findings.title: Task 1.4 mentions adding only `kind` to existing emits; the universal spine also requires `next_recommended` and `final_assessment` which are missing from existing archive emits
findings.description: The MODIFIED orbit-conventions `Internal-run JSON summary format` requirement (specs/orbit-conventions/spec.md:7-16) declares 6 spine fields REQUIRED on every run-summary JSON across all kinds, including `final_assessment` AND `next_recommended`. Verified against the existing archive emit at openspec/changes/archive/2026-05-18-bootstrap-openspec-orbit/.orbit-runs/archive-2026-05-18T19-16-06Z.json: it has NEITHER `final_assessment` NOR `next_recommended`. After this change lands, archive emits MUST include both per the universal spine — but task 1.4 only mentions adding `kind` to existing emits (review, address-reviews, archive, inline audit-drift). For review and address-reviews this is OK in practice (their actual emits already include both fields de facto, even though the schema docs don't list them). For archive it is NOT — the archive emit will violate the universal spine on the very next archive run after this change lands. Recommendation: expand task 1.4 (or add task 1.5) to explicitly require adding `final_assessment` and `next_recommended` to the archive SKILL.md emit instructions, with archive-specific recommendation rules (e.g., 'archive complete; change moved to openspec/changes/archive/<YYYY-MM-DD>-<name>/'). Optionally define a verify-time check in task 9.5 to confirm post-change archive emits carry the full spine.

findings.title: MODIFIED orbit-conventions spine requirement doesn't extend the baseline `.orbit-runs/ per-change persistence` requirement to cover the two new persistence paths (`openspec/explore/<name>/.orbit-runs/` and `openspec/.orbit-runs/`)
findings.description: The baseline `Requirement: .orbit-runs/ per-change persistence` at openspec/specs/orbit-conventions/spec.md:135-157 says 'The system SHALL define `openspec/changes/<change-name>/.orbit-runs/` as the per-change iteration history directory' — singular, only the changes/<name> path. This change introduces TWO additional persistence locations: (a) `openspec/explore/<name>/.orbit-runs/` for explore named-mode emits (per orbit-run-summary-emit spec.md:5,23) and (b) `openspec/.orbit-runs/` for project-wide audit-drift emits (per spec.md:361). Both are explicitly invoked by the new requirements but neither is documented in the baseline persistence requirement, and the MODIFIED `Internal-run JSON summary format` requirement only modifies the SHAPE, not the LOCATION. A reader of orbit-conventions/spec.md alone would conclude the only valid `.orbit-runs/` location is under `openspec/changes/<name>/`. Recommendation: either (1) extend the MODIFIED delta to ALSO modify the `.orbit-runs/ per-change persistence` requirement (broaden it to enumerate the 3 valid root paths with their respective scoping rules), or (2) add a new ADDED requirement to orbit-conventions like `.orbit-runs/ persistence locations` that enumerates all three. The address-reviews schema reference doc already documents the dual whole-repo path (openspec/.orbit-runs/) but orbit-conventions's spec doesn't. This is a real cross-doc coherence gap that propagates into archive-time staleness if not closed.

findings.title: `/opsx:continue` completeness definition is hand-rolled and may drift from upstream `openspec status --json` `isComplete` semantics
findings.description: The `Propose-shaped recommendation logic` requirement defines /opsx:continue's complete state as 'proposal.md + design.md + tasks.md + at least one specs/<capability>/spec.md all present' (spec.md:198). But the actual upstream openspec-continue-change SKILL.md (verified via grep) uses `openspec status --json`'s `isComplete: true` field to gate completion. The upstream definition may include more artifacts (e.g., for non-spec-driven schemas) or fewer (e.g., schemas where specs/ are optional). Hand-rolling the artifact check in the emit-layer risks drift from upstream's authoritative definition. Recommendation: replace the hand-rolled list with a reference to upstream's `openspec status --json` `isComplete` field, OR add a scenario explicitly testing that the emit-layer's completeness check matches `isComplete: true` from upstream — so future schema additions don't silently break the recommendation logic. Minor — current logic works for the default spec-driven schema, but the spec should be schema-agnostic.

findings.title: Apply per-chunk-end emission spec doesn't specify what happens when chunks span MORE than 2 groups, or when the preamble syntax is malformed
findings.description: The chunk preamble example shows `Chunk N (groups X)` and `Chunk N (groups X-Y)` covering 1-2 groups (and 2 consecutive groups). The format spec at spec.md:215 reads `Chunk N (groups X[-Y]): <chunk-name>` which only encodes a range, not arbitrary group sets. Two underspecified cases: (a) what if a chunk spans 3+ non-consecutive groups (e.g., `Chunk 4 (groups 6,8,9)`)? (b) what if the preamble has a typo or missing required fields (e.g., `Chunk 2 groups 3-4:` with missing parens)? The current spec falls back to 'no-chunking apply' (rule 3) only when the preamble is absent — not when malformed. An implementer might either (i) silently fall back to no-chunking on malformed preamble, or (ii) error out, or (iii) partially parse. Recommendation: add a brief 'Malformed preamble handling' note: either error and refuse to emit (loud failure surfaces the bug), or fall back to single-emit-at-session-end (graceful degradation). Also note explicitly whether non-range group sets are supported or not. Minor — practical projects use simple ranges, but the spec should be unambiguous.

findings.title: Lifecycle per-kind extensions list `sync_specs` but this field maps to a deprecated upstream command (openspec-orbit#6 will remove)
findings.description: The orbit-conventions MODIFIED delta lists lifecycle extensions as: `archive_path, audit, sync_specs, unresolved_markers, user_decision`. The archive-summary-schema.md confirms `sync_specs` is currently in the archive emit. However, the change's own design.md (line 15) and proposal.md (line 15) reference openspec-orbit#6's removal of `/opsx:sync-specs` (deprecated upstream, absorbed by `openspec archive` in v1.3.1). When #6 ships, `sync_specs` may stop being a meaningful field in the archive emit (or be repurposed). Codifying `sync_specs` in the orbit-conventions universal spine list locks a soon-to-be-stale field into the canonical convention spec. Recommendation: either (1) drop `sync_specs` from the orbit-conventions lifecycle extensions list and let the archive SKILL.md document it as a transitional field, or (2) add a note: 'sync_specs persists from pre-#6 architecture; will be removed/renamed when #6 lands' so future readers understand the lineage. Trivial impact — but the same forward-look-discipline that D8 / Requirement: No forward-look at other-issue future behavior changes applies in reverse: avoid baking in fields that other open issues will remove.

fresh_pass_assessment: Fresh-context same-model (Opus 4.7, clean conversation) produced 5 findings (0 CRITICAL, 2 WARNING, 3 SUGGESTION) that survived pushback against the iter-1 internal + iter-1 external resolutions. F1 (archive emit incomplete spine) and F2 (persistence-requirement gap) are both genuine cross-doc coherence issues neither prior cycle surfaced — F1 because the in-context cycle anchored on `kind` as the only missing field and the external cycle anchored on the `findings_summary` T0 edge case (EW2) but didn't trace the spine through to `final_assessment`/`next_recommended` for archive specifically. F2 is a missed baseline-vs-delta coherence check (the MODIFIED delta modifies SHAPE but leaves PERSISTENCE location requirement untouched, which is now inconsistent with the new emit paths). This is meaningful empirical evidence that --fresh (clean context, same model) provides anchor-break value distinct from both in-context and cross-AI: the fresh pass entered without any priors about which gaps were 'already handled' and could re-examine the spine-vs-persistence axes that neither prior pass explored. The 3 SUGGESTION-tier findings (F3/F4/F5) are polish-level and could plausibly have been caught by either prior cycle but weren't — consistent with anchoring suppressing low-rank concerns once the high-severity issues are resolved.
